summary:
This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) Part 75 focuses on the critical importance of choosing words carefully in both speech and thought. Sheikh Ali Mashhour explains that speech is the physical articulation of internal thoughts, and words carry profound spiritual effects on both the listener and Sh. Ali Mashhour. The lecture emphasizes that words are serious matters—they can reinforce beliefs (including false ones), shape the heart, and influence actions. Drawing from Quranic examples, Sh. Ali Mashhour illustrates how lying repeated can lead to self-deception, and how the phrasing order in Quranic verses prevents momentary misconceptions.

Sh. Ali Mashhour establishes three criteria for good speech: the statement must be good in itself (truthful and honest), appropriate in its time, place, and manner, and beneficial in its effects on the listener. He emphasizes that not all truths are appropriate to speak—backbiting is cited as an example of true but sinful speech. The principle of Taskhiyah (purification) before Tajmil (beautification) is explained as foundational to proper communication and understanding. The lecture concludes by addressing modern speech problems, particularly excessive profanity and vulgarity in contemporary culture, and advocates for conscious control of thought as the foundation for purified speech.
